title: Why Doesn't the Space Station Fall? 🛰️ #shorts
description:
The International Space Station orbits only about 250 miles up, where Earth's gravity is still about 90 percent as strong as at the surface. So why doesn't it fall? It does: it's falling all the time. Throw a ball sideways and it curves to the ground; throw it faster and it lands farther away. At about 17,500 mph, the ground curves away as fast as the station falls, so it keeps missing Earth. That's why astronauts float: they're not beyond gravity, they're in free fall along with the station. A whisper of air at that altitude slowly drags the station down, so about once a month it fires thrusters to climb back up.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
